title: 22.1 A 0.275pJ/b 42Gb/s/pin Clock-Referenced PAM3 Transceiver Tolerant to Supply Noise, Reference Offset and Crosstalk for Chiplets and Short-Reach Memory Interfaces
problem: Chiplet and short-reach interfaces using single-ended PAM3 face challenges: large reference-voltage generators, TX-RX reference mismatch, supply-noise-induced jitter (SSN coupling), and crosstalk sensitivity (2x vs NRZ).
motivation: Multi-chip modules (MCMs) and die-to-die (D2D) interfaces demand high bandwidth density with minimal power, but PAM3 signaling introduces noise and reference-offset sensitivities that degrade margin.
method: A clock-referenced PAM3 transceiver uses reference-tracking techniques to reject TX-RX offset, supply-noise immunity circuits to handle SSN coupling, and crosstalk-resilient signal design, achieving 0.275pJ/b at 42Gb/s.
key_novelty: Clock-referenced receiver tracking TX reference variations to eliminate TX-RX reference-offset issues in single-ended PAM3.
contributions: Clock-referenced PAM3 receiver eliminating reference-voltage generators
Reduced crosstalk sensitivity in PAM3 signaling

metrics.noise_tolerance: supply noise up to hundreds of mV

limitations: Abstract-only; bit error rate (BER), voltage margins, area/power breakdown, and comparison with other noise-tolerant PAM3 designs not provided.
primary_theme: Noise-tolerant clock-referenced PAM3 for chiplet interconnects
